implementation_policy: Coupled native solve of a 57.6 g tennis ball (rigid sphere, r = 33.5 mm, 8 m/s forward) striking a tensioned 12.8 m tennis net: 3.5 mm polyethylene strands on a 45 mm mesh as a float64 tensile centreline beam network with finite bending stiffness and Kelvin-Voigt loss (effective E = 25 MPa; geometry fixed, so EA and EI scale with E), a pretensioned steel headline (finite-compliance XPBD) inside the bound headband, bottom and laced side bindings, and a finite folded 45 mm PET centre strap with an implicit strip material, anchored at the court socket; hard unilateral ball/strand and band-triangle contacts are solved in the same constrained Newton step, advanced at dt = 1/153600 s on the CPU with the frozen contact library (assets scenes/tennis_net_hit/frozen/webbing_revision.so, sha-pinned in physics/common.py) and recorded at 3840 Hz. The source runs 0-4 s from the common gravity-prebalanced packet; each edit restores the bit-exact float64 state of its own accepted 0-3 s solve and continues to 4 s with only its DSL-resolved change (ball forward speed x0.2 / x2, net strand modulus x0.1 / x10); DELETE removes net, strap and anchors and solves the free ball against the court/fence triangles (court_collision/rigid_with_court.so). physics/qualify.py checks frame clocks, protected inputs, contacts and court clearance and writes render_cache.npz. appearance/render.py replays the 96 genuine frame-centre states and the linear 3840 Hz shutter samples in the packed court scene (fixed camera, 1/480 s centred shutter) within 1 um; appearance/realism.py applies the current look through one audited hook. --stage verify checks the accepted native delivery (renders/tennis_net_hit/accepted) and the published suite named in scene_manifest.json. Materials are effective values, not calibrated against a measured net.
